source.title: Towards Monosemanticity: Decomposing Language Models With Dictionary Learning

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a linkpost summary, not the longer paper it links to.
record.tranche_reason: As a summary of the original work, it reports a qualitative result from varying the number of learned features.
record.gate_note: The post reports that smaller feature sets give a coarse view and larger sets reveal subtler properties. It gives no split examples, input partitions, or directional similarities. Other reported findings on interpretability, steering, and feature universality do not test the listed splitting versions. Comments are not treated as study results.
record.test_reason: This is the authors' linkpost summary of Towards Monosemanticity, an original source for V1. It reports the original's resolution-knob finding, so its relation is the original test itself. Because it is an original source, it gets no verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The number of learned features acts as a resolution knob: few features give a coarse view, many give a refined view. The authors also say features are largely universal across models, and that scaling to frontier models is the next challenge.
record.recipe_differences: The post says the authors varied the number of learned features, but does not give the training or measurement details needed to establish the full recipe.
record.problems: The size comparison is qualitative and lacks exact dictionary sizes, split examples, input-coverage measurements, and direction similarities. The post identifies the demonstrated model as small.
record.rows_left_out: No additional splitting results are reported in the supplied post. Other claims about interpretability, steering, and feature universality were omitted because they do not report the splitting behavior in the listed versions.

untested.parts: In this summary text: that finer features partition the coarse feature's inputs and lie near its direction (the full paper's feature-splitting section is not supplied).
All; only a small one-layer model is studied, and scaling is named as future work.
All; no nested families or geometry are reported in the post.
All; a commenter's speculation about SAE artifacts is not a study result.

missing.what: The full paper's feature-splitting section (split examples, feature-family geometry, dictionary-size runs) is only linked, not included in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: This study is an original source (Towards Monosemanticity), so no verdict labels are given. The supplied text is a blog or linkpost summary plus comments; the comments (e.g. Raemon quoting 'fail gracefully', Tom Angsten on artifacts) are not treated as results. The reader's tranche T1 is nominal; the item is better treated as the original's own summary than as a replication.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not state that several finer features partition a coarse feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
No result tests whether splitting holds in large models or open SAE releases.
No nested feature families, geometric closeness, or concept hierarchy is tested.
No parent-child firing or intervention involving SAE size or sparsity is tested.
No decomposition of larger latents into smaller latents or novel-latent analysis is reported.
No test attributes splitting to the sparsity objective or compares objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.size_stated: A layer with 512 neurons; more than 4000 features
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of learned features

conditions.value: small set versus large set; exact sizes not stated

rows.measure: Qualitative resolution of the feature representation
rows.baseline: A small set of features gives a coarse view
rows.value: A large set of features gives a more refined view that reveals subtle properties
rows.locator: Post body, paragraph beginning “Finally, we zoom out”
rows.note: The post provides only this qualitative comparison; it does not describe whether the finer features cover the coarse feature's inputs or how their directions compare.
rows.check: Link and state are acceptable for a summary: 'more features' gives a 'more refined view', but finer features covering a coarse feature's inputs or lying near its direction are not stated. The row restates the original source's own result, so it cannot ground a verdict. Subject should be the one-layer small transformer's MLP layer (512 neurons), not 'not stated'.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
